comments.content: Perhaps a simple solution will be to do a timeout in five seconds if you can't find some type of failure event.

It might also be worth trying to reproduce based on the RPC I specified in the Telegram chat. 
As long as it looks presentable thats my main concern. Seems like too much text to try and cram in.

Related thread https://t.me/UbiquityDAO/31131/32216
My phone wallet had an RPC that seems to have gone down. When I clicked to claim it would infinite hang with no wallet prompt. 
We should catch this and notify the user that there are issues with the in wallet selected RPC and suggest the top pick from our RPC handler package.  
![image](https://github.com/ubiquity/pay.ubq.fi/assets/4975670/c67e4bc9-c028-4bc8-8138-ca853e870881)
Code seems fine. Although I'm not entirely sure what the best way to test this is. @rndquu can you take a quick review to finalize this pull?
What's the input?
Why did you rename this?
What is this used for? This doesn't seem to be the right approach to me.

You are assuming it is a mobile browser based on the media query. 
I'm sure there is a better way to do this in typescript.
WebKit browsers by default allow for six concurrent tcp connections last I researched. Consider doing multiples of six for optimal speed.
Why seven seconds?
I'm surprised we used media queries in the typescript code at all. It really doesn't seem to be the best way to detect if it's mobile browser.

```typescript
  const isTouchScreen = 'ontouchstart' in window || navigator.maxTouchPoints > 0;
```
I'm sure there are npm modules that handle this check robustly. I don't think it makes sense to rely on the media query in a javascript runtime.

Make the logs way less verbose. You shouldn't show every test unless its happening very slowly (it shouldn't)  
Also for the RPC that works- can you make it a clickable link to pre-fill the network details on MetaMask? I'm pretty sure i've seen this capability on Chainlist.org etc.
In this case I would display something more like:
...and thats it. 
gnosis.drpc.org should be a link to pre-fill all the RPC information on MetaMask.
What is your conclusion on the solution here?

Given that they have [167 open sev2-normal issues](https://github.com/MetaMask/metamask-mobile/labels/Sev2-normal) and given that it took them two weeks to close out [the only `sev0-urgent` issue](https://github.com/MetaMask/metamask-mobile/issues/5128) I wouldn't hold my breath on it. 
So then lets just accomodate users to be able to manually copy and paste the values and be done with this.
